title: Countable Postnikov extension and comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. A complex in $\mathcal T$ indexed by $\mathbf N$ is a sequence $\cdots\xrightarrow{d_3}X_2\xrightarrow{d_2}X_1\xrightarrow{d_1}X_0$ with $d_{r-1}d_r=0$. A Postnikov system for it means $Y_0=X_0$, distinguished triangles
$$Y_r\xrightarrow{a_r}X_r\xrightarrow{b_r}Y_{r-1}\xrightarrow{c_r}Y_r[1]\quad(r\ge1),$$
with $a_{r-1}b_r=d_r$ (and $a_0=1$). The connecting arrows give a sequence $Y_0\to Y_1[1]\to Y_2[2]\to\cdots$.
If $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(X_i[i-j-2],X_j)=0$ for all $i>j+2$, such a system exists; more precisely every finite Postnikov system on an initial segment can be extended to the next term under these vanishings.
Suppose $u_r:X_r\to X'_r$ is a map of complexes, both complexes are equipped with Postnikov systems, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(X_i[i-j-1],X'_j)=0$ for all $i>j+1$. Here a map of (finite or full) Postnikov systems extending $u$ is a family $g_r:Y_r\to Y'_r$ with $g_0=u_0$ such that, for each $r\ge1$, $(g_r,u_r,g_{r-1})$ is a morphism of the distinguished triangles above: $a'_rg_r=u_ra_r$, $b'_ru_r=g_{r-1}b_r$, and $g_r[1]c_r=c'_rg_{r-1}$, where $c_r:Y_{r-1}\to Y_r[1]$ and $c'_r$ are the connecting arrows. Then every map of the initial finite Postnikov systems extending the corresponding $u_r$ extends to the next term. Thus there is a compatible map of the full systems extending $u_r$. If every $u_r$ is an isomorphism, all its maps $Y_r\to Y'_r$ can be chosen to be isomorphisms. These assertions also apply to finite complexes by appending zero terms.

source.place: Tag 0D7Z (definition-postnikov-system); Tags 0D83 (lemma-existence-postnikov-system), 0D82 (lemma-maps-postnikov-systems-vanishing) and 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle). Countable form obtained by the extension induction in their proofs; no coproduct or convergence assertion is included.

proof.text: First propagate the two stated vanishing hypotheses through the already chosen finite systems. For the existence hypothesis put $s=2$ and $A_j=X_j$, $Z_j=Y_j$; for the comparison hypothesis put $s=1$ and $A_j=X'_j$, $Z_j=Y'_j$. Fix $i$ and prove $\operatorname{Hom}(X_i[(i-j-s)],Z_j)=0$ by induction on $j$ with $i>j+s$. At $j=0$ this is the hypothesis because $Z_0=A_0$. For $j>0$, inverse-rotate the distinguished triangle to $Z_{j-1}[-1]\to Z_j\to A_j\to Z_{j-1}$. A map $f:X_i[(i-j-s)]\to Z_j$ has zero composite to $A_j$ by the assumed vanishing. The cited Hom exactness factors $f$ through $Z_{j-1}[-1]$. Its group of possible factors is isomorphic, by shifting both arguments, to $\operatorname{Hom}(X_i[i-(j-1)-s],Z_{j-1})$, which vanishes by induction. Thus $f=0$. This induction applies to every prescribed finite system, without making or changing any of its choices.

source.place: Tags 0D82 (lemma-maps-postnikov-systems-vanishing), proof (1), and 0D83 (lemma-existence-postnikov-system), obstruction vanishing; Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological).

proof.text: For extension to $n=1$, put $b_1=d_1:X_1\to Y_0=X_0$ and use TR1 and inverse rotation (TR2) to complete it to $Y_1\to X_1\xrightarrow{b_1}Y_0\to Y_1[1]$. For extension to $n=2$, the prescribed triangle $Y_1\xrightarrow{a_1}X_1\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0\to Y_1[1]$ satisfies $b_1d_2=d_1d_2=0$. The Hom exactness gives $b_2:X_2\to Y_1$ with $a_1b_2=d_2$. Complete $b_2$ to the required triangle by TR1 and TR2. Both constructions keep all previously prescribed triangles.

source.place: Tag 0D81 (lemma-postnikov-system-small-cases), proof for lengths 1 and 2; Tag 0D83 (lemma-existence-postnikov-system), initial cases.

proof.text: Now let $n\ge3$ and retain a prescribed system through $n-1$. Put $h=b_{n-1}d_n:X_n\to Y_{n-2}$. Its composite with $a_{n-2}$ equals $d_{n-1}d_n=0$. Inverse rotation of the triangle at $n-2$ and Hom exactness therefore factor $h$ through $Y_{n-3}[-1]$. The factor is zero: by shifting, its Hom group is $\operatorname{Hom}(X_n[1],Y_{n-3})$, which is the case $i=n$, $j=n-3$, $s=2$ of step 1. Hence $h=0$. Apply Hom exactness to the prescribed triangle $Y_{n-1}\xrightarrow{a_{n-1}}X_{n-1}\xrightarrow{b_{n-1}}Y_{n-2}\to Y_{n-1}[1]$ to obtain $b_n:X_n\to Y_{n-1}$ with $a_{n-1}b_n=d_n$. Complete $b_n$ to a distinguished triangle $Y_n\to X_n\to Y_{n-1}\to Y_n[1]$ using TR1 and TR2. This extends the given system by exactly one term.

source.place: Tag 0D83 (lemma-existence-postnikov-system), extension induction and its two Hom-exactness obstruction factorizations; Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological).

proof.text: For comparison, suppose a prescribed map of systems is given through $n-1$ and write $\alpha=g_{n-1}b_n-b'_nu_n:X_n\to Y'_{n-1}$. For $n=1$ this is zero since $g_0=u_0$ and the $u_r$ commute with $d_1,d'_1$. For $n\ge2$, compute $a'_{n-1}\alpha=u_{n-1}a_{n-1}b_n-a'_{n-1}b'_nu_n=u_{n-1}d_n-d'_nu_n=0$. Inverse rotation of the target triangle at $n-1$ and Hom exactness factor $\alpha$ through $Y'_{n-2}[-1]$. The factor vanishes by step 1 with $i=n$, $j=n-2$, $s=1$, since $\operatorname{Hom}(X_n,Y'_{n-2}[-1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X_n[1],Y'_{n-2})=0$. Thus $g_{n-1}b_n=b'_nu_n$ for every $n\ge1$. Apply the cited second-square form of TR3 to the two prescribed triangles at $n$, with second and third vertex maps $u_n,g_{n-1}$. It supplies $g_n:Y_n\to Y'_n$ satisfying both $a'_ng_n=u_na_n$ and $g_n[1]c_n=c'_ng_{n-1}$. Together with the computed square these are precisely all three required equations, and the earlier $g_r$ are retained.

source.place: Tag 0D82 (lemma-maps-postnikov-systems-vanishing), proof (2): difference of the second square and TR3 after rotation; Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological).

proof.text: If all $u_r$ are isomorphisms, $g_0=u_0$ is an isomorphism. Inductively the morphism of distinguished triangles $(g_n,u_n,g_{n-1})$ constructed in step 4 has two isomorphism components, namely $u_n$ and $g_{n-1}$. The cited triangle two-out-of-three statement implies that $g_n$ is an isomorphism. The same induction shows that any already prescribed finite comparison has isomorphism components under these hypotheses.

Starting from $Y_0=X_0$, recursively choose one extension supplied by steps 2 and 3 for each successive natural number, always retaining the preceding choices. The data at any index are fixed at the first stage containing that index, so all triangles and equations hold in the resulting countable system. Starting from $g_0=u_0$, the identical recursion with step 4 produces a compatible full comparison; it may start with any prescribed finite comparison. This is ordinary countable recursive choice of objects and morphisms in a fixed ambient universe, not a limit construction. The connecting maps in the asserted sequence are exactly $c_{r+1}[r]:Y_r[r]\to Y_{r+1}[r+1]$. For a finite complex append zero objects and zero differentials. New vanishing conditions whose source index exceeds the old length hold since that source is zero; all other conditions are unchanged. Apply the countable result and restrict to the original finite segment. If finite comparisons are componentwise isomorphisms, extend $u$ by the unique isomorphism of zero objects and apply step 5.

source.place: Tag 0D7Z (definition-postnikov-system), recursive definition; example-key-postnikov, explicit infinite extension of the notion; countable recursion on the extensions proved above.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0D82 and 0D83, extension proofs, with the small cases in Tag 0D81 and triangle isomorphisms in Tag 014A; countable recursive assembly written explicitly.
